newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Telstra cable past 1.5 mln Australian homes.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Telstra cable past 1.5 mln Australian homes.

text.p: Telstra Corp said on Thursday its optic fibre cable network had now past 1.5 million homes.

"In terms of our definition of homes which are able to be connected, we have past one and a half million homes and we can service those," Telstra Multi-Media chief Gerry Moriarty told Reuters in an interview.
The cable network is being used by Telstra and its joint venture partner News Corp Ltd to operate their Foxtel pay television operations.

Moriarty doubted Optus could reach its original target of three million homes by 1998 -- a goal since superseded by Optus Vision's announcement that it would accelerate its cable roll-out and pass two million homes by the end of 1996.

"He (Optus Vision chief executive Geoffrey Cousins) has declared victory when he has cabled only a third of what he announced," he said, referring to Cousins' announcement on Thursday that Optus cable had past well over a million homes.
"He says they are going to finish Sydney at the end of 1996 and finish Melbourne and Brisbane by April next year," Moriarty added.
"If you interpret the figures (released on Thursday), he certainly can't get to three million homes."
Telstra, which is spending A$4 billion on its broadband cable roll-out, aims to pass four million homes by mid 1999.
"We are absolutely on target," Moriarty said.
